finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated into the query. Prepared statements are not used, and ORDER BY cannot be parameterized anyway. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL expressions, for example a boolean or CASE subquery that works as a blind oracle to read other tables. SQLite's PDO driver rejects stacked queries, but subqueries still work.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort)

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' takes attacker input with no validation
$sort is concatenated into the SQL string and run with PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting or escaping on this path. The sibling function list_users_safe (lines 9-13) uses an allowlist map, but list_users_sorted does not call it. There is no authentication check in the file. find_user (line 15) uses a prepared statement and is safe.

verdict.guard_found: none on list_users_sorted; the allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) is a separate function that is never called from it
verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 reads $_GET['sort'] directly and concatenates it into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query with no allowlist, cast or authentication check, so any caller of list_users_sorted exposes the injection; the only caveat is that no caller of list_users_sorted exists in this directory, so reachability depends on code outside it.
